scope: Diagnosis of real_application_expected_429 and real_application_held_expected_408 from tls-response-eof-unresolved.json: scripts/rest-body-wire.py --tls through the pinned Caddy to the real application, called by scripts/test-caddy-ingress.py --backend-port. Also the probe change for those two reads.
claim_limit: The mechanism is reproduced locally with the real application, the pinned Caddy binary and the unmodified probe. That each of the two recorded CI occurrences was this mechanism is inferred: neither of those runs captured partial reply bytes. The later occurrence in ci_recurrence captured the complete reply, but not the hold state. The changed probe had not run in CI when this record was written.
summary: Both observations fit the Go net/http post-handler body drain that 72641d1 diagnosed for the synthetic early rejection. Caddy relays the real application's complete 429 or 408 with Connection: close. It then reads the unfinished 128-byte declared body before closing: until the 20-second request_body deadline, or with no deadline after a race. The 3-second denied reader fails on both hold states. The 23-second held reader fails only on the hold without a deadline. Under CPU contention, the unmodified probe failed in this lab at both reads with the same TimeoutError after receiving the complete reply; the changed probe did not fail.

confirmed: Locally, behind the pinned Caddy, the real application's header-only 429 arrives complete with Connection: close, and Caddy then holds the connection in the post-handler body drain (see local_reproduction.contention_run).

Under CPU contention, 716 of 7760 denied requests got EOF 19.9842-20.01 s after the complete 429 (body_deadline_hold) and 8 got no EOF within 26 s (deadline_free_hold); the 3-second reader would fail on 724.

The unmodified rest-body-wire.py --tls, looped through the pinned Caddy under contention, failed 28 times at this denied read with TimeoutError; its diagnostic line shows the complete 429, Connection: close and receive_phase awaiting_recv_eof (local_reproduction.ci_faithful_ab).

The eight 502 resets are a consequence of the timeout, not its cause: closing a held TLS socket whose session tickets were never read sends RST, and the pinned Caddy logs the same readfrom ... connection reset by peer 502 error for it.
inferred: The CI denied request got its complete 429 and then waited in one of the two hold states. A 3-second timeout cannot tell which; the 20-second hold is far more frequent in this lab.
unknown: Whether the CI 429 was received at all: ce2da74 logged no partial bytes. The Caddy log cannot settle it. A denied request left unanswered for 3 s and then closed produced no Caddy log line in 5 of 5 local runs, so the absence of a ninth error line is uninformative.

confirmed: Locally, behind the pinned Caddy, the real application's 408 after its 15-second body deadline arrives complete with Connection: close. Under CPU contention, 3 of 6208 held requests then got no EOF within 26 s; the proxy closed within 0.0031 s once the client sent close_notify.

Goroutine dumps taken during two of those held holds each show exactly one deadline-free drain. The server goroutine is in finishRequest -> body.Close -> io.CopyN -> tls.(*Conn).Read, and the writeLoop in writeBody's deferred Close waits on that same body's mutex. The dump-time ss shows both ends established, the 408 sent 26 s earlier, and a keepalive timer only.

In the A/B run, the unmodified rest-body-wire.py --tls failed 1 time at a held 408 read (case=public_tls_held_6_of_8 request=POST /api/v1/passkeys/login/start). The TimeoutError came after the complete 408 with Connection: close (receive_phase awaiting_recv_eof), and the process ran 38.337 s. In CI the TimeoutError came about 38 s after the held requests were sent (about 17:08:01.2Z to 17:08:39.33Z).
No held request hit the 20-second body-deadline hold (0 of 6208). That deadline is set at the request start, so such a hold would end about 5 s after the 408, inside the 23-second reader.

If the application never answers, the pinned Caddy answers itself at the 20-second body deadline (504, or an empty 200) with Connection: close and then EOF. The CI reader would have raised AssertionError about 17:08:21Z, not TimeoutError at 17:08:39.33Z.
inferred: The CI held socket got its complete 408 and then waited in the deadline-free hold. This is by elimination: a 408 with a deadline-bound hold passes; socket 1 getting no reply would time out about 17:08:24.5Z; any held socket getting no reply would draw Caddy's own 20-second reply. The local reproduction matches the signature exactly: 408 at about 15 s, no EOF, and a TimeoutError 23 s later, both with the harness and with the unmodified probe.
unknown: Which held index and route failed, and the partial bytes: 16a7dc0 printed no diagnostic for held reads.

mechanism.same_as: docs/evidence/experimental-rebuild/caddy-ingress-receive-diagnostics.json (72641d1): response.finishRequest calls conn.r.abortPendingRead() then reqBody.Close(), and body.Close drains up to 256 KiB of the unfinished body before the connection closes.

states_with_real_application.observed: EOF within 0.007 s (denied) and 0.0131 s (held) of the complete reply under contention.

Denied: EOF 19.9842-20.01 s after the complete 429, at the request_body read_timeout set when the request started. Dumps: server goroutine draining while the writeLoop waits on the body mutex in its first body read.
states_with_real_application.why_not_held: Inference from the source: by the 408 the writeLoop has waited 15 s in a body read, so abortPendingRead always finds a read to abort and clears the deadline. Either way the request_body deadline would end such a hold about 5 s after the 408.

states_with_real_application.observed: No EOF within 26 s of the complete reply, and the proxy closed within 3.1 ms after the client's close_notify.
states_with_real_application.goroutine_order: In all four dumps the server goroutine holds the body mutex and drains with no deadline, while the writeLoop waits on it in writeBody's deferred Close. This is the reverse of the order in 72641d1's deadline_free_hold, where the writeLoop drained and the server goroutine waited. The effect is the same: abortPendingRead has already cleared the read deadline when the drain read starts.
states_with_real_application.ordering_basis: Inferred from the Go source plus the dumps; no execution trace recorded the interleaving.

source_references.fact: abortPendingRead sets a past read deadline only while a read is in progress, waits for it, then clears the deadline.
body.Close holds body.mu and, with doEarlyClose, drains with io.CopyN up to maxPostHandlerReadBytes (256 KiB).
transferWriter.writeBody's deferred Close closes the request body after a body read error.
request_body sets the connection read deadline to now + read_timeout (20 s for the REST matcher).
The application rejects from headers with 429 when the per-IP or global body admission is full, and with 408 when to_bytes exceeds the admission timeout; reject() adds Connection: close on HTTP/1.

contention_run.dump_reading: Every draining server goroutine (finishRequest -> body.Close -> io.CopyN -> tls.(*Conn).Read, IO wait) pairs with exactly one writeLoop blocked on the same body mutex: the lockSlow address equals that *body pointer + 0x2c. In each dump exactly one pair has its writeLoop in writeBody's deferred Close, meaning its body read had been aborted: that is the hold without a deadline. Every other pair has a writeLoop that never started its body read, which is a body-deadline hold. In the held dumps, no denied deadline-free hold was open at dump time; this is estimated from row order (rows are written as each socket finishes, about 11 rows/s, and the nearest denied deadline-free holds ended about 17 s before or began about 18 s after).

behavior: read_closed takes unfinished_body=False. Only the denied 429 and held 408 reads pass True, and only a TLS stream (the request went through Caddy) takes the new path.

On that path it reads until the shared helper classifies the reply as Content-Length complete, and asserts strict completeness and Connection: close. It then closes its own TLS side (close_notify via unwrap) and requires the proxy's close_notify and TCP EOF within the same socket timeout: 3 s denied, 23 s held.
BrokenPipeError or ConnectionResetError at the close step is accepted: the proxy had already closed when the client's close_notify arrived.
A receive or close OSError prints the existing diagnostic line, now with phase=response or phase=close, and re-raises the original error.
probe_change.rationale: RFC 9112 section 9.6 asks a client that receives Connection: close to close after reading the response. Section 9.5 asks a client whose body is unwanted to stop sending it and close. Go's server inside Caddy may wait for that client close while draining. The probe no longer depends on the proxy closing first, but still fails when the reply is incomplete or wrong, or when the proxy does not close promptly after the client does.
no_longer_required: Proxy-initiated closure before the client closes, for the denied and held reads through TLS Caddy.
stricter_than_before: Through TLS Caddy, the denied and held replies must be Content-Length complete with Connection: close before the client closes.
unchanged: The direct application run (plain TCP), which still requires the application's own EOF for every read

related.production_note: The application closes promptly; the holds are in the proxy. In production, the same race can hold an HTTP/1 connection after the application's 408 or 429, until the request_body deadline or, without a deadline, until the client sends data or closes. docs/PRODUCTION_OPERATIONS.md already states this for 408, 413 and 429. No product policy was changed.
